title: SpecASR: Accelerating LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition via Speculative Decoding
problem: LLM-based ASR suffers from high decoding latency due to autoregressive generation, challenging real-time requirements; existing speculative decoding ignores ASR-specific characteristics and achieves limited speedup.
motivation: LLM-based ASR offers high accuracy and multi-dialect support, but decoding latency is the critical bottleneck for real-time speech recognition applications.
method: SpecASR uses speculative decoding (a small, fast model predicts the next words, then a large model verifies them) to speed up speech-to-text. Because both models hear the same audio, they predict the same words much more often than language tasks without audio. To reduce wasted predictions, SpecASR adjusts how many words the small model predicts based on verification rates, recycles failed predictions, and checks only likely candidates instead of all possibilities during verification.
key_novelty: Speculative decoding adapted for speech-to-text that exploits how both models naturally agree when processing the same audio, using adaptive draft length and prediction recycling to minimize wasted work from the fast model.
contributions: Observation of high output alignment in ASR despite intermediate mismatches
Adaptive draft sequence generation dynamically tuning draft length
Draft sequence recycling strategy reusing previously generated sequences
Two-pass sparse token tree generation for latency balancing
3.04x-3.79x speedup vs autoregressive, 1.25x-1.84x vs SOTA speculative decoding
limitations: Not discussed; focus is on ASR-specific optimization.
primary_theme: Audio-conditioned speculative decoding for LLM-based ASR acceleration
